title: Kubernetes CronJob
description: Kubernetes Job is a controller that creates one or more pods and ensures that a specified number of them successfully terminate. Kubernetes Job can be used to run containers that perform finite tasks for batch jobs. Kubernetes CronJob is used to schedule Jobs. Attackers may use Kubernetes CronJob for scheduling execution of malicious code that would run as a container in the cluster.

data_components.name: Scheduled Job Creation
data_components.definition: Creation of Kubernetes CronJob or Job resources in the cluster API, recording the schedule expression, pod template spec, and requesting principal - the definitive signal for T1053.007.
relevant_events: Kubernetes audit event: verb=create, apiGroup=batch, objectRef.resource=cronjobs - record schedule, image, and requesting user
Kubernetes audit event: verb=create, apiGroup=batch, objectRef.resource=jobs (direct job creation without CronJob parent)
Kubernetes CronJob spec fields indicating abuse: schedule='*/1 * * * *' (every minute), restartPolicy=OnFailure, image outside approved registry

data_components.name: Scheduled Job Modification
data_components.definition: Modification of existing CronJob schedules or pod templates to inject malicious containers or change execution frequency, indicating an attacker hijacking an existing legitimate CronJob for persistence.
relevant_events: Kubernetes audit event: verb in [update, patch], apiGroup=batch, objectRef.resource=cronjobs - diff of spec.schedule or spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers
Kubernetes audit event: verb=delete, apiGroup=batch, objectRef.resource=cronjobs (deletion could be cleanup after malicious execution)
Change to CronJob's serviceAccountName field to use a higher-privileged service account

data_components.name: Application Log Content
data_components.definition: Kubernetes API server audit logs providing full context for CronJob/Job lifecycle events, including the requesting principal, source IP, and full resource spec for forensic analysis.
relevant_events: Kubernetes audit log: full request body for verb=create on batch/cronjobs containing malicious image and privileged pod spec
Kubernetes event: SuccessfulCreate for Job triggered by CronJob, showing which node the workload ran on
Kubernetes audit log: GET or LIST on cronjobs by a service account that should not be enumerating scheduled jobs

detection_strategies.name: Detection of Malicious Kubernetes CronJob Scheduling
detection_strategies.summary: AN0582 specifically detects abuse of container orchestration platforms where adversaries create CronJobs to maintain persistence or execute malicious Jobs across the cluster. Confirmed STIX object targeting T1053.007.

vendor_detections.title: CronJob created or modified by non-CI principal
vendor_detections.intent: Surface every Kubernetes audit event creating or updating a batch/v1 cronjobs resource. Adversaries plant cron-style persistence because the schedule guarantees re-execution even after the original entry vector is patched.
vendor_detections.query:
// Wiz Threat Center / Kubernetes Audit Log query (Resource Graph style)
KubernetesAuditLog
| where verb in ("create", "update", "patch")
  and objectRef.apiGroup == "batch"
  and objectRef.resource in ("cronjobs", "jobs")
| where user.username !in~ (
    "system:serviceaccount:argocd:argocd-application-controller",
    "system:serviceaccount:flux-system:source-controller"
  )
| project requestReceivedTimestamp,
          principal = user.username,
          namespace = objectRef.namespace,
          name      = objectRef.name,
          schedule  = requestObject.spec.schedule,
          image     = requestObject.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image
required_telemetry: Audit policy at RequestResponse for batch/* resources
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Backup tooling, certificate-renewal jobs, and metric-collection cron tasks fire here legitimately. Allowlist by namespace+name pattern.
vendor_detections.limitations: API-server-mediated only. If an adversary writes a static-pod manifest with a sleep loop, this rule does not see it (separate detection on MS-TA9017).

vendor_detections.title: Falco: K8s CronJob with non-trivial schedule outside platform namespaces
vendor_detections.intent: Fire on CronJob creation events where the schedule is unusual (very frequent, e.g. less than 5 minutes) or the namespace is outside the platform set, indicating likely adversary persistence rather than legitimate batch work.
vendor_detections.query:
- macro: frequent_schedule
  condition: ka.req.cronjob.schedule contains "*/1 " or ka.req.cronjob.schedule contains "*/2 " or ka.req.cronjob.schedule contains "* * * * *"

- list: platform_cronjob_namespaces
  items: ["kube-system", "cert-manager", "velero", "backup-system"]

- rule: Suspicious CronJob Created
  desc: A K8s CronJob was created with an unusually-frequent schedule, or in a non-platform namespace by a non-CI principal.
  condition: kevt and kcreate and ka.target.resource="cronjobs"
             and (frequent_schedule or not (ka.target.namespace in (platform_cronjob_namespaces)))
  output: >
    Suspicious CronJob created
    (user=%ka.user.name name=%ka.target.name ns=%ka.target.namespace
     schedule=%ka.req.cronjob.schedule images=%ka.req.cronjob.images)
  priority: WARNING
  source: k8s_audit
  tags: [k8s, mitre_persistence, T1053.007]
required_telemetry: Audit policy capturing requestObject for batch/* at RequestResponse level
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Tight-schedule CronJobs are sometimes legitimate (health-check probes implemented as cron). Tune frequent_schedule by environment; consider correlation with image-allowlist.
vendor_detections.limitations: ka.req.cronjob.* fields require k8saudit plugin v0.5+ and audit policy that captures requestObject for cronjobs.

vendor_detections.title: CronJob creation hunt with schedule frequency scoring
vendor_detections.intent: Hunt for CronJob create/update events in the audit log lake. Score each by schedule frequency (more frequent = higher risk) and by namespace (non-platform namespace = higher risk).
vendor_detections.query:
WITH cron_events AS (
  SELECT
    event_time,
    cluster_name,
    user_username AS principal,
    object_namespace AS namespace,
    object_name AS cronjob,
    request_object:spec:schedule::string AS schedule,
    request_object:spec:jobTemplate:spec:template:spec:containers[0]:image::string AS image,
    verb
  FROM K8S_AUDIT.PUBLIC.EVENTS
  WHERE verb IN ('create', 'update', 'patch')
    AND object_resource = 'cronjobs'
    AND object_apigroup = 'batch'
    AND event_time >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
)
SELECT
  *,
  CASE
    WHEN schedule LIKE '* * * * *' THEN 5
    WHEN schedule LIKE '*/1 %'     THEN 4
    WHEN schedule LIKE '*/2 %'     THEN 3
    WHEN schedule LIKE '*/5 %'     THEN 2
    ELSE 1
  END AS frequency_score
FROM cron_events
WHERE namespace NOT IN ('kube-system', 'cert-manager', 'velero')
ORDER BY frequency_score DESC, event_time DESC;
required_telemetry: K8s audit logs landed in Snowflake
Audit policy capturing requestObject for batch/cronjobs
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Frequent-schedule probe-style cronjobs can score high without being malicious. Combine with image-not-on-allowlist for a stronger signal.
vendor_detections.limitations: Lake latency, schema assumed as standard normalized form.

mitre_cross_references.name: Cron
mitre_cross_references.rationale: The Azure Kubernetes Sigma rule 'azure_kubernetes_cronjob' is tagged T1053.003 (Cron) rather than T1053.007 (Container Orchestration Job). This reflects the fact that Kubernetes CronJob semantics are modeled on Unix cron, and several SIEM vendors and rules authors apply T1053.003 when detecting K8s CronJob events. Defenders tuning alerts on T1053.003 may miss K8s-specific CronJob detections tagged at T1053.007, and vice versa.

mitre_cross_references.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
mitre_cross_references.rationale: A Kubernetes CronJob ultimately executes a container that runs a command or script (T1059). MITRE T1053.007 describes it as 'scheduling deployment of a Job that executes malicious code.' The command execution inside the job container maps to T1059 (parent) or T1059.004/T1059.013 specifically. A detection covering only the Job creation (T1053.007) misses the payload execution inside the container.
